chapter_title: Tracking Mastery: xAPI, Learning Record Stores, and MicroSims
learning_objective: The learner will judge whether each of eight requests to see or use a student's learning record should be allowed, allowed only with an agreement and family notice, or not allowed, correctly judging at least seven of eight on the first attempt.
specification:
Type: microsim **sim-id:** who-may-see-this-record
**Library:** p5.js
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Evaluate
**Bloom Verb:** judge
**Learning Objective:** The learner will judge whether each of eight requests to see or use a student's learning record should be allowed, allowed only with an agreement and family notice, or not allowed, correctly judging at least seven of eight on the first attempt. **Template:** https://github.com/dmccreary/health-education/tree/main/docs/sims/trusted-source-sorter
**Prerequisites:** learning record, student-controlled data and its five parts, data portability (all defined in the section "Data Portability and Student-Controlled Data" above). **Evidence of Mastery:** For each of 8 requests, the learner chooses one of three responses and submits it. A response is correct when it matches the "Correct response" column in Content. Mastery is 7 of 8 correct on the first attempt. Reading the five principles is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) Anyone at the school may see any student's record. (2) A vendor may use records for any purpose once it has them. (3) A family may only look at the record, never take a copy. **Instructional Rationale:** Judging a request requires applying the principles of minimum necessary access and stated purpose to a concrete case. Cases from teachers, parents, vendors, researchers, and advertisers show that the same record deserves different answers for different requesters and purposes. **Content:** Three responses, shown for every request: | Response | Meaning shown | |---|---| | Allow | A person with an educational need, or the student's own family, may see or take the record | | Allow only with an agreement and family notice | An outside party may use the record only under a written agreement that states the purpose, with the family notified | | Do not allow | The use has no educational need or goes beyond the stated purpose | Eight requests: | # | Request shown to the learner | Correct response | Why (shown as feedback) | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | A teacher views the mastery records of the students in her own class to plan next week. | Allow | The teacher has a direct educational need for her own students. | | 2 | A teacher with no connection to a class looks up the records of its students out of curiosity. | Do not allow | There is no educational need, so access is not justified. | | 3 | A parent asks to see their own child's learning record. | Allow | Parents have the right to inspect their child's education records. | | 4 | A student moving to a new school asks for a copy of their record in a standard format. | Allow | Data portability lets the record follow the student. | | 5 | The software vendor wants to use identifiable student records to train a new commercial product. | Do not allow | The use goes beyond providing the service the school bought. | | 6 | A university team, working under a district-approved study, asks for class-level summaries with no student names. | Allow only with an agreement and family notice | An outside party may use data only under a written agreement stating the purpose. | | 7 | An advertiser asks for a list of students who are struggling in math. | Do not allow | Student records must never be used for advertising. | | 8 | A district-approved tutoring partner asks to see one student's fractions mastery to prepare a session. | Allow only with an agreement and family notice | An outside party with an educational purpose needs an agreement and notice. | **Provenance:** The responses follow the five principles in the chapter section "Data Portability and Student-Controlled Data," which are recommended design practice, not a statement of any one law. The requests are illustrative, written for this chapter, and the sim must say that legal duties are covered in Chapter 10. **Rules:** Each request has exactly one correct response, given in Content. A request is scored on its first submitted response only. The score counts first-attempt correct responses out of 8. Mastery is a score >= 7. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner sees one request at a time and the three responses. 2. The learner chooses a response and submits it. The sim marks it correct or incorrect and shows the feedback text. 3. If incorrect, the learner may choose again; the second attempt does not change the score. After the second attempt, the correct response and reason are shown. 4. After all 8 requests, the sim shows the score and lists misjudged requests with their correct responses. 5. The learner should notice that three requests are allowed, two need an agreement, and three are refused, and that the requester's job title alone never decided the answer. **Feedback:** 8 requests, shuffled once per session, two attempts each. Correct: "Correct: [response]. [Why text]." Incorrect: "Not quite. [Why text for the correct answer, without naming the response]." After the second attempt the correct response is revealed and the request counts as missed. A running score "First-try correct: n of 8" is shown. Final message for a score >= 7: "You can judge who should see a student's record." For a score < 7: "Review the five principles and try again; the requests will be reshuffled." **Starting State:** Request 1 of the shuffled order is shown with the three responses, the score "First-try correct: 0 of 8," and the prompt "Should this request be allowed?" **Chapter Anchors:** The chapter lists five principles: minimum necessary, see it, take it, limit it, remove it. The chapter states that outside parties may see identifiable records only under a written agreement for a stated purpose, and never for advertising. The mastery bar is 7 of 8.
